name.text: Building a binomial with a given coefficient

questiontext.text:
Give a binomial of the form \((p + qx)^4\), where \(p\) and \(q\) are non-zero whole numbers, such that the coefficient of \(x^{@tp@}\) in its expansion is \({@tg@}\). There is more than one correct answer.

Type it as a bracket to the power 4, for example (5-2*x)^4.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The row for power 4 is 1, 4, 6, 4, 1. In \((p + qx)^4\) the term in \(x^2\) is \(6p^2(qx)^2\) and the term in \(x^3\) is \(4p(qx)^3\), so the coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(6p^2q^2\) and the coefficient of \(x^3\) is \(4pq^3\).

[[if test="is(tp=2)"]]

Here \(6p^2q^2 = {@tg@}\), so \(p^2q^2 = {@m^2@}\) and \(pq = {@m@}\) or \(pq = {@-m@}\).

[[else]]

Here \(4pq^3 = {@tg@}\), so \(pq^3 = {@m@}\).

[[/if]]

Two answers are \({@sampd@}\) and \({@samp2d@}\). Changing the sign of both \(p\) and \(q\) also works, for example \({@neg1d@}\), because \((-p - qx)^4 = (p + qx)^4\).

questiondescription.text:
Binomial Expansions: building a binomial with a given coefficient

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.2: Construct (p + qx)^4 with a given coefficient of x^2 or x^3; any correct bracket is accepted.

node.description: Row number times p times q only

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(tp=2)"]]

Your bracket has \(6 \times {@pp@} \times {@qq@} = {@tg@}\), but in \((p + qx)^4\) the term in \(x^2\) is \(6p^2(qx)^2\): both \(p\) and \(q\) are squared. Your bracket gives \({@got@}x^2\).

[[else]]

Your bracket has \(4 \times {@pp@} \times {@qq@} = {@tg@}\), but the term in \(x^3\) is \(4p(qx)^3\): \(q\) is cubed. Your bracket gives \({@got@}x^3\).

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Your bracket gives coefficient \({@got@}\). In \((p + qx)^4\) the coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(6p^2q^2\) and of \(x^3\) is \(4pq^3\). Choose \(p\) and \(q\) that make it \({@tg@}\).
